$comment: LANGUAGE-NEUTRAL IDENTITY FIXTURES. Read by BOTH engines' test suites:
so Python and Node cannot drift into two different answers about which
players are the same instrument. A page that disagrees with a report has
shipped on this repo for weeks before.
EVERY PAIR IS PINNED AS A STRING, deliberately, and not read off the
published bundle. A bundle-only test is how the GLM slug collision below
stayed green: the bundle cannot contain the offending pair until the bad
url has already shipped. Both halves are here -- known-EQUAL pairs that
must merge and known-DIFFERENT pairs that must not -- because a grouping
function that merges everything and one that merges nothing both pass a

slug_identity.$comment: A DECLARED instrument is already in familySlug's output shape, so familySlug is the identity on it. This is what makes the collision below unconstructible for declared instruments rather than merely untested.

cases.name: glm-non-thinking-vs-thinking
cases.why: THE CASE THIS DESIGN EXISTS FOR. Same weights file, thinking off vs thinking on. Their player_version strings differed only by / vs - before the separator was repaired, and familySlug squeezes every non-alphanumeric run to '-' so BOTH slug to local-gguf-glm-4-7-flash-ud-q4-k-xl -- ONE url for two players, with familyBySlug returning the first match. normaliseVersion keeps them distinct, which is why checking only that function gives a false all-clear: two of three consult seats did exactly that on 2026-09-16. Repairing the separator does not help; the desktop repaired it and the strings became IDENTICAL, because player_version labels weights. Only a declared instrument separates them.

cases.name: glm-after-the-separator-repair
cases.why: The same two players after the desktop repaired the separator. The version strings are now byte-identical, so every function that reads only the version says 'one player'. The declaration is the only thing that still separates them.

cases.name: qwen-reasoning-ladder-baseline-vs-thinking
cases.why: +0.24 to +0.28 mean score apart, the largest single effect measured in this corpus, under ONE identical player_version.

cases.name: gpt-oss-reasoning-effort-ladder-low-vs-medium
cases.why: A deliberate dose-response experiment on reasoning effort. Keyed on player_version its three levels render as one row, and mean_placing averages an experiment's own levels into one sort key.

cases.name: gpt-oss-reasoning-effort-ladder-medium-vs-high
cases.why: The second rung of the same ladder. Pinned separately so a fix that separated only the end points would still go red.

cases.name: nemotron-base-vs-thinking
cases.why: Same weights, enable_thinking false vs true. Same shape as the Qwen and gpt-oss ladders on a different vendor's switch.

cases.name: gemma-community-quant-vs-qat-q4-0
cases.why: Measured on the desktop: two independently sourced Q4_0 builds emit a bit-identical twelve-answer set while the community UD-Q4_K_M build of the same weights emits seven distinct answers to the same twelve documents, and the Q4_0 pair both collapses on publication-bias and beats the community build on p-curve and z-curve. Different quantizations of one model are different instruments. NEGATIVE CONTROL for the slug collision: these two do NOT collide, so a test that reported a collision here would be reporting a broken comparison rather than a defect.

cases.name: haiku-dated-vs-undated-snapshot
cases.why: KNOWN-EQUAL. The case the datestamp strip was written for: eighteen Haiku players declare claude-haiku-4-5 and the nineteenth declares claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. They must merge -- and under a declared instrument they merge because both entries DECLARE claude-haiku-4-5, not because a regex happened to remove the right eight characters.

cases.name: one-instrument-across-two-arenas
cases.why: KNOWN-EQUAL. A player_id is a model IN ONE ARENA, so one instrument holds one id per arena. This is the merge /players exists to perform, and it must survive every change that separates the pairs above.

cases.name: grobid-one-tool-five-arena-harnesses
cases.why: KNOWN-EQUAL across player TYPES too. Five Grobid player ids are one tool at one version playing five arenas through five adapters; before the declared instrument, tools were keyed by player_id and rendered as five separate rows.

cases.name: groq-vs-openrouter-route-to-one-model
cases.why: KNOWN-DIFFERENT. Same weights reached two ways; the route measurably changes results (token ceilings, quantisation, sampling defaults), and the OpenRouter entry additionally pins the Cerebras backend.

cases.name: docpluck-academic-vs-standard
cases.why: KNOWN-DIFFERENT. A deliberate A/B of two configurations that were measured separately; one row labelled 'docpluck' would report one configuration's number under the other's name.

cases.name: cohere-command-a-vs-command-r-plus-datestamps
cases.why: KNOWN-DIFFERENT, and the reason the datestamp strip has to stay conservative: -03-2025 and -08-2024 are snapshots of DIFFERENT models, not of one. Stripping both still leaves cohere/command-a and cohere/command-r-plus distinct -- pinned so a future widening of the regex goes red here rather than in production.

cases.name: undeclared-falls-back-and-is-not-merged-with-a-declared-one
cases.why: The fallback path. A player whose registry entry declares no instrument keys on the normalised version, which is a DEGRADED key; it must not be quietly folded into a declared row that happens to sit nearby.

inference_config.$comment: Canonicalisation cases for framework/identity.py inference_config + its Node mirror. `entry` is a registry entry fragment; `expect` is the canonical config, and `expect_sha_null` says whether the digest must be null (which it is exactly when the config is null -- never the hash of the string 'null').

cases.name: max-tokens-is-a-budget-not-a-configuration
cases.why: Correcting an output ceiling must not mint a new instrument. The ceiling is recorded in provenance.request_max_tokens on every record, so nothing is lost by excluding it here -- and including it would have split gpt-oss-20b into two instruments when the Cohere ceilings were corrected.

cases.name: no-knobs-at-all-is-null-not-an-empty-config
cases.why: An R tool has no temperature. Returning {} would assert a configuration nobody measured; null says 'this player exposes no inference settings to us', which is a different and true claim.

cases.name: a-budget-only-body-is-still-no-configuration
cases.why: An entry whose only extra_body key is the ceiling configures nothing about the model.

cases.name: nested-blocks-canonicalise-by-key-order
cases.why: chat_template_kwargs is a nested object, and two entries that wrote its keys in a different order must hash equal or the audit would report a split that does not exist.

cases.name: a-zero-temperature-is-a-setting-not-an-absence
cases.why: 0.0 is falsy in both languages. A truthiness check here would drop the one sampling parameter every local player sets.
